extracted.intended_audience: early stage investigators applying for the Stephen I. Katz Early Stage Investigator R01 (NIA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance / sample text for the 'Change in Research Direction' attachment required for the Stephen I. Katz Early Stage Investigator R01; shows how to describe prior work, the new conceptual and methodological directions, specific aims tied to the new direction, and how the proposal differs from prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / high-level requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the R01 Stephen I. Katz Early Stage Investigator Research Project Grant, NIA supports an innovative project in an area of science that represents a change in research direction for an early stage investigator and for which no preliminary data exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the proposed project is both an innovative project and represents a bona fide change in research direction for an early stage investigator; the solicitation expects no preliminary data for the new direction. Refer to the NIH Application Guide and the current Notice of Funding Opportunity when preparing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: State previous research clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: My previous research examined auditory perception and cortical signal processing in humans, nonhuman primates (NHPs), and mice (non-disease models) primarily using auditory psychophysical tasks, acute single-unit recordings, and optogenetic manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize prior research focus, species/models used, and main methods so reviewers can judge how the new direction differs and what relevant expertise you bring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement of the new research direction and overall goal
rubrics_metrics.description: My new research direction is to understand mechanisms linking sensory deprivation to cognitive impairment and hippocampal (HC) dysfunction, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology. ... My new research direction thus focuses on neural pathology and activity in HC rather than sensory cortex, with the overall goal of understanding a disease process rather than normal function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate succinctly how the proposed research departs conceptually from prior work and state the overarching goal (e.g., disease process rather than normal function).

rubrics_metrics.name: New conceptual directions: state specific questions/aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The current aims thus reflect a fundamentally new conceptual direction, as reflected by four general questions: (1) Does HL accelerate accumulations of Aβ and p-tau in a mouse model of AD? (2) Does HL induce or exacerbate pathophysiological outcomes in HC including spontaneous hyperactivity and/or diminished SWRs? (3) Does HL induce changes in functional connectivity between HC and ACtx, and are these changes transient or long-lasting? (4) Are HL‑induced changes in AD pathology, HC physiology, and/or CI dependent upon sex?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out concrete research questions or aims that embody the conceptual shift (tie them to Aims where appropriate, e.g., Aim 1 and Aim 2) so reviewers can see how the project tests the new direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: New methodological directions: enumerate and justify new methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed work will require six new methods: (1) assessment of disease progression in a mouse model of AD, (2) histological assessment of AD pathology (Aβ and p-tau accumulations) using iDISCO methodology, which includes multiplexed immunolabeling, tissue clearing, light‑sheet microscopy, and algorithmic whole‑brain quantification, (3) induction of HL by cochlear ablation, (4) chronic recordings with high‑density Neuropixels probes, (5) assessment of CI with a spatial learning and memory task, and (6) assessment of altered functional interaction between HC and ACtx using Granger causality analysis to quantify changes in the strength and directionality of influence between areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the new experimental/analytical techniques required by the new direction, and provide enough methodological detail to convince reviewers the approach is feasible or that necessary expertise will be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare to prior work and explain differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The closest link to my prior work is that I have recent experience with a partial HL model (moderate single‑sided HL through noise exposure). However, the proposed technique is somewhat different (complete HL via cochlear ablation vs. partial HL via noise exposure), and the motivating questions and goals of understanding disease progression are fundamentally different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state similarities and differences between prior and proposed work, so reviewers can judge novelty and the extent of the shift in direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate relevance of prior experience and risk mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: My background knowledge, including dynamics of neural activity changes following HL, is thus relevant to the current proposal and directly influenced important aspects of the proposed experiments. Finally, my experience inducing and measuring HL mitigates one methodological risk associated with this new research direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the project lacks preliminary data, describe how prior skills/experience, relevant knowledge, or preliminary related work reduce methodological or feasibility risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure the attachment with clear section headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample attachment uses the headings: NEW RESEARCH DIRECTIONS; New conceptual directions; New methodological directions; Comparison to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the Change in Research Direction attachment into clear sections addressing prior work, the new direction, conceptual questions/aims, methodological changes, and comparison to prior work to make the case explicit and easy to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align specific Aims to the new direction with mechanistic hypotheses and planned measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In Aim 1, I will determine whether HL accelerates AD pathology by surgically deafening mice carrying AD‑related transgenes, and then examining hallmark AD symptoms at histological level (accumulations of amyloid β [Aβ] and phosphorylated tau [p‑tau]) and physiological level (neuronal hyperactivity, diminished memory‑related network oscillations (sharp‑wave ripples [SWRs])). In Aim 2, I will examine a putative mechanism of HL‑induced CI by longitudinally tracking neuronal activity in HC before and after HL, testing for changes including hyperactivity, SWR abundance, and functional interaction between HC and ACtx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how each Aim directly tests hypotheses tied to the new conceptual direction and list the primary outcome measures and analyses that will address those hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer applicants to official application instructions and additional samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Please be sure to refer to the NIH Application Guide and the current Notice of Funding Opportunity when preparing an R01 application. Find more NIA sample applications and information about training and career development: https://www.nia.nih.gov/research/training/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH/NIA procedural instructions and consult additional sample applications and FOA text to ensure compliance with formatting, content, and eligibility rules.
